proponi.title: Propose a project – ideaBlume
proponi.res_title: Do you do research at the University of Turin?
proponi.res_text: You can apply to the co-funding programme with your group's project. You need a financial goal, a clear use of funds and a permanent staff member as principal investigator.
proponi.ext_title: Do you represent an association, a school or an organisation?
proponi.ext_text: You cannot launch a campaign on your own, but you can propose an idea to carry out with a research group: the ideaBlume Office looks for the right group and puts you in touch.
time: Applications to the programme: once a year. For the {edizione} edition: {candidature}.
Reply to a partnership proposal: within 10 working days, by phone or email.
Costs: proposing a partnership is free and groups selected by the programme pay no fees. {link:come-funziona.html#costi|Read how much it costs}.
proponi.examples_title: Examples of projects with the local community
proponi.examples: The project {link:progetto-scienza-doposcuola.html|“Science workshops in neighbourhood after-school clubs”} was started by associations in Barriera di Milano and Falchera together with the Department of Philosophy and Education Sciences.
proponi.res_path_title: If you do research: from idea to campaign
proponi.res_path_intro: Applications to the {link:programma.html|University programme} open once a year. Here is what happens, step by step.

res_path.d: You need a financial goal, a use of funds explained item by item, rewards the group can really deliver and a permanent staff member as principal investigator.
The form takes about 10 minutes and your data stays saved while you fill it in. For the {edizione} edition, applications run {candidature}.

res_path.t: Take part in the training and selection
res_path.d: At the meetings you learn how to explain your project and run a campaign. A University committee then chooses the projects based on quality, impact and feasibility.

res_path.t: Prepare the page with the Office
res_path.d: The ideaBlume Office helps you with text, rewards and budget. Every text must be written in Italian and in English.
Fundraising lasts {dmin} to {dmax} days. If you reach the goal, the University adds the same amount, up to {tetto}.

proponi.ext_path_title: If you represent an organisation: from idea to partnership
proponi.ext_path_intro: Local associations, schools, organisations and businesses can start a project together with the University. Sending a proposal is free and does not commit you to anything.

ext_path.d: Fill in the form, explaining which problem you would like to tackle and who would benefit. You do not need scientific expertise.
Within 10 working days someone from the ideaBlume Office contacts you, by phone or email.
The Office looks for a University of Turin group interested in the idea and puts you in touch. Together you decide whether and how to take it forward.

The research group leads the project and the organisation takes part as a partner. It has already happened with the after-school science workshops, started by associations in Barriera di Milano and Falchera.

proponi.tips_intro: Donors usually do not know the subject and want to understand quickly why the project matters. These four points help with both the application and the campaign.

tips.d: Explain in a few sentences which problem you are tackling and who it matters to. If someone who does not know the subject understands it, you are on the right track.
Ask for the amount you really need and explain every expense: together they must add up exactly to the campaign goal.
Decide from the start what you will be able to show donors, even while the work is under way: data, photos, small milestones.
A postcard or a lab visit is enough, as long as the group can really deliver it. Anyone who prefers can always make a free donation.

proponi.groups_title: For groups with an ongoing campaign
proponi.groups_intro: Is your campaign online? Here is how to keep it alive and who to turn to when you need help. For any question you can write to the Office: {email_programma}.

groups.d: Send text and photos to the Office: we publish them within 2 working days in the project's “Updates” section. Even a small step forward helps your supporters feel part of the work.
Write each text once in Italian and once in English, in two separate fields: the site shows one language at a time. The title can be up to 80 characters, the subtitle up to 160.
Messages sent with “Write to the group” come straight to you. We tell people who write that you usually reply within {giorni} working days.
Ask the Office to add a second goal with an amount and a purpose: it will appear in the box next to “Support”. Donations above the goal are not matched by the University.

If the goal is reached, write to people who chose a reward to ask for their address, if needed. When the work is finished, send the report with the actual spending: we publish it on the project page and send it to supporters.
For a mistake on the project page or another problem with the site, {link:contatti.html#scrivici|write to us with the contact form}, choosing “Problem with the site”.

proponi.doubts: You can find more answers in the {link:faq.html#promotori|questions for people proposing a project}. For the programme you can write to {email_programma_link}, for partnerships to {email_collaborazioni_link}.

chi.title: About us – ideaBlume

what.d: We publish only projects by research groups at the University of Turin. Before publication we review each page with the group, so that anyone can understand the project without knowing the subject.
We check each group's budget and rewards before publication: every expense must be clear and realistic, and together they must add up exactly to the campaign goal.

We run the {link:programma.html|University co-funding programme}. We support the selected projects during the campaign and, if they reach their goal, the University adds the same amount, up to {tetto} per project.

We ask every group for updates during the work and a final report with the actual spending. We publish it on the project page and send it to the donors, so everyone can see what their contribution achieved.

chi.money: If the goal is reached, the money goes to the group's department, earmarked for the project: it cannot be used for anything else. Every project page shows how the funds are used, item by item, and, once the work is finished, the report with the actual spending.
chi.story_intro: We started with a simple question: what happens to good ideas that are too small for a major grant, but too useful to stay in a drawer?

story.d: During a break in the department, a researcher mentions giving up on a study because she was a few thousand euros short of the sensors she needed. Others around the table have similar stories. Over the following weeks that conversation becomes a list of stalled projects and a proposal to the University: ask people directly for help.

The ideaBlume Office is born: three people and a shared desk. The name joins «idea» with «Blume», German for flower, because an idea only blooms if someone looks after it. That same year we write the rule we still follow, «all or nothing»: if the goal is not reached, donations go back to the donors.

With {link:progetto-robot-anziani.html|«Social robots for older people's independence»}, the site and the first edition of the {link:programma.html|University programme} start together: if a project reaches its goal, the University adds an amount equal to the goal. The group passes its target and we see that the idea works.

story.t: The neighbourhood, and the first missed goal
story.d: With {link:progetto-scienza-doposcuola.html|the after-school science workshops}, associations from Barriera di Milano and Falchera build a project together with the University: the start of our {link:collabora.html|partnerships with local organisations}. That same year, {link:progetto-rifugi-frane.html|the risk map for mountain huts} misses its goal. We return the donations and say so clearly on the project page: that too is part of our promise to donors.

Very different projects reach the site, from {link:progetto-matematica-accessibile.html|maths formulas readable with a screen reader} to {link:progetto-plastica-batteri.html|bacteria that break down microplastics}. Alongside first-time donors, more people follow every update and come back to support a new project.
We redesign the site starting from donors and researchers: clearer text, accessible pages, a complete English version and the same numbers on every page.

We have published {n_progetti} projects. {sostenitori} supporters have donated {raccolto} and the University has added {cofin}. Applications for the {edizione} edition of the programme run {candidature}.

chi.what_intro: We stand between the labs and the people who want to support them. Our work starts before a campaign goes online and ends only when the group has accounted for its spending.
chi.money_no: If the goal is not reached, donations go back to the donors. Only the payment fee, which you always see before confirming, is not returned. You can find all the details in the {link:faq.html|FAQ}.
chi.people: ideaBlume is run by the University's ideaBlume Office. From the original three people we have grown into a team of seven with different skills: former researchers who help groups prepare their campaigns, people who look after accounts and reports, people who work on the text and people who answer the phone and email. If you write to us, we reply within {giorni} working days.
chi.hours: Opening hours: {orari}. You can also {link:contatti.html#scrivici|write to us from the site}.
chi.next: Every project on the site started like that conversation over coffee. You can support an ongoing campaign or, if you have an idea, propose it to us.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions – ideaBlume
faq.count_0: No questions match. Try another word or {link:contatti.html|write to us}.
faq.not_found: Call us on {tel_link} ({orari}) or write to {email_aiuto_link}. We reply within {giorni} working days.

q.q: Can I donate without choosing a reward?
a: Yes. Choose “Free donation” and enter the amount, from {min} upwards.
Rewards are just a thank-you: they are not required.

q.q: What is the minimum amount?
a: {min} for a free donation, for every project.
For a reward, the minimum is the price shown next to it.

q.q: Do I need to register to donate?
a: No. We only need your name, surname and email for the confirmation.

q.q: How can I pay and how much does it cost?
a: You can pay by: {metodi}.
The payment provider charges a fee, which you see in the summary before confirming (1.8% + €0.35 by card, PayPal or Satispay). There is no fee from us for bank transfers.

q.q: My payment did not go through: what should I do?
a: Nothing has been charged. You can try again straight away: the details you entered stay saved.
Try another payment method, for example a bank transfer.
If the problem continues, call us on {tel_link} ({orari}): we will help you complete the donation.

q.q: What happens if the project does not reach its goal?
a: We return your donation: this is the all-or-nothing rule.
The refund goes back to the same payment method within 15 days of the end date. The payment fee is not refunded.

q.q: The project has already reached its goal: is it still worth donating?
a: Yes, as long as the campaign is open. Extra donations go to the second goal shown in the project box.
Donations above the goal are not matched by the University.

q.q: How does the University match work?
a: If a programme project reaches its goal, the University adds an amount equal to the goal, up to {tetto}. This is also called co-funding.
{link:programma.html#raddoppio|Read an example}.

q.q: Can I donate anonymously? Who sees my name?
a: Yes: in the form choose “Donate anonymously”. The public sees “Anonymous supporter”.
The research group still receives your name and email to thank you and send your reward. The amount is never public.

q.q: Will I get a receipt? Is the donation tax-deductible?
a: Yes: after donating you receive the summary and the tax receipt by email.
Donations to the University are tax-deductible: keep the receipt for your tax return.

q.q: When will I get my reward?
a: After the campaign closes, if the goal is reached. The group will write to ask for your address, if needed.

q.q: Who can propose a project?
a: Research groups at the University of Turin, with a permanent staff member as principal investigator.
{link:proponi.html|Read who can propose}.

q.q: We are an association or a school: can we take part?
a: Yes, as a partner of a research group: {link:collabora.html|propose a partnership}. The ideaBlume Office looks for the right group.
Sending the proposal does not commit you and is free.

q.q: When can we apply?
a: Once a year, through a call. For the {edizione} edition: {candidature}.

q.q: How much does it cost to propose a project?
a: Proposing a partnership is free.
Groups selected by the programme pay nothing either: training, support and publication are paid for by the University.

q.q: How long does a campaign last?
a: {dmin} to {dmax} days.

q.q: How do we publish updates and the final report?
a: Send text and photos to the Office ({email_programma}): we publish them in the project's “Updates” section.
At the end we ask for a report with the spending, which we also send to supporters.

q.q: Do we have to write content in two languages?
a: Yes, in Italian and in English, in separate fields: the site shows one language at a time. {link:proponi.html#gruppi|Read the guidance}.

q.q: Who runs ideaBlume?
a: The University of Turin's ideaBlume Office. {link:chi-siamo.html|About us}.

q.q: How do I know the money really goes to research?
a: Every project publishes the use of funds item by item and, at the end, a report with the actual spending.
The money goes to the group's department, earmarked for the project.

q.q: How can I talk to a person?
a: Call us on {tel_link} ({orari}) or write to {email_aiuto_link}.

q.q: Crowdfunding
a: Raising money online: many people donate small amounts to make a project happen.

q.q: Goal
a: The minimum amount the project must raise by the end date. If it is not reached, donations are returned.

q.q: All or nothing
a: The ideaBlume rule: the group receives the money only if the goal is reached by the end date. Otherwise we return your donation.

q.q: Second goal
a: A higher amount, with a specific purpose, for projects that have already reached their goal. Donations above the goal go to it.

q.q: Supporter
a: Someone who donates to a project.

q.q: Research group
a: The University people who propose and carry out the project. The principal investigator leads the group.

q.q: Reward
a: A small thank-you from the group for people who donate at least a certain amount, for example a postcard or a lab visit. It is not required.

q.q: Free donation
a: A donation without a reward, of the amount you prefer, from {min} upwards.

q.q: Fee
a: The cost charged by the payment provider (card, PayPal, Satispay). You see it before confirming your donation.

q.q: University programme
a: The initiative through which the University selects some projects, supports them and co-funds them.

q.q: Year (edition)
a: The year in which the campaign took place. For programme projects it is the programme edition.

q.q: Final report
a: The text in which the group describes the results and how it spent the money.
